supported_conclusions: The 20 larger classes have exactly the counts expected from a 50000-row stratified sample.
The four rarest classes were expanded from 61 combined rows to 615 combined rows, producing the final total of 50554 rows.
Every unique sampled record originates from the full processed dataset.
The rare-class expansion involved replacement-based repeated selections.
limitations: The exact common-class row multiset was not reproduced from original_data.csv using train_test_split with random_state=42.
The precise historical intermediate input ordering or source snapshot is therefore not recoverable from the currently archived files.
The reconstruction supports the class-count procedure but not an exact row-for-row regeneration.
revision_protocol_note: The referee-driven revision experiments do not reuse the historical 50554-row sampling procedure. They use the reconstructed, duplicate-aware, group-disjoint O3 cohort and frozen random and chronological split assignments.
